definition.sound: Professional, once itinerant Tashelhit poet-singers of the Sous leading small troupes: the leader sings his poetry (amarg) line by line over the one-string ribab fiddle and lotar lute, and a chorus answers.
markers: One-string ribab fiddle and lotar lute over a metal naqus struck with a rod
Leader sings a line, the chorus repeats it
Pentatonic melodies in five-beat (5/8) and other compound cycles
Set order: instrumental astara opening, sung poem and dance, closing tabbayt that speeds up and stops dead

origin.text: Korea (regional styles: Gyeonggi around Seoul, Namdo in the south-west, Seodo in the north-west)

definition.sound: Korean folk song: strophic songs with a refrain, from anonymous village and work songs to the polished popular repertoire of professional singers, set to cycling rhythmic patterns (jangdan) and sung in sharply different regional styles.
markers: Same tune for each verse, with a refrain such as 'Arirang, arirang, arariyo'
Rhythmic cycles such as gutgeori, jajin-taryeong and semachi
Regional colour: bright Gyeonggi songs, rich and dramatic Namdo songs, free-rhythm laments of the north-west
